title: Is the TI LP-MSPM0L1306 the right board for my project?
short: A LaunchPad development kit for TI's MSPM0L1306: a 32 MHz Arm Cortex-M0+ with 64 kB of flash, 4 kB of RAM, two op-amps, and a light sensor and thermistor on the board. Per MHz it is as fast as the bigger MSPM0G3507; RAM is what limits it, so every program has to be sized for 4 kB first.

meet.what: A LaunchPad development kit for TI's MSPM0L1306 microcontroller, with the XDS110 debug probe built in: one USB cable powers it, flashes it and carries its serial port. It has three buttons (one is reset), a red LED, an RGB LED, a light sensor wired through op-amp 0, and a thermistor.
facts: Arm Cortex-M0+, 32 MHz from the internal oscillator (measured 32.16 MHz)
12-bit ADC, 2 op-amps, 1 general-purpose amplifier, a comparator with an 8-bit DAC, CRC, 3 DMA channels
TI MSPM0 SDK: DriverLib examples only (no FreeRTOS or TI Drivers examples for this chip)
Chip yes, board no (Zephyr 4.4.2); the test board file works

projects.t: Blink an LED with TI's SDK
projects.result: Build 3.3 s, flash 0.6 s with OpenOCD (15.0 s with TI's UniFlash)
On an out-of-tree board file; Zephyr has none for this LaunchPad. 94% of RAM used by hello_world

projects.result: TI's out-of-box demo answers MessagePack commands: light 339 to 343 counts at the desk, 435 to 445 on a later check; board 21.9 to 22.8 °C

projects.t: Small AI model in 4 kB of RAM
projects.result: 8k-parameter room-occupancy model, 20 of 20 test vectors right, 84 to 100 ms; the 30k model does not fit
CMSIS-DSP from TI's SDK: 256-point FFT in 2.25 ms, 32-tap FIR on 64 samples in 1.0 ms, answers checked against the Mac
Blink, 11 tasks, task switch 12 to 16 µs; TI offers no example for this chip
Reads -165 °C with this chip's factory calibration; about 21.7 °C with the manual's typical value
14 of 19 fit and run, 13 pass their own check; 5 need more RAM than the chip has
micro-ecc signs in 0.50 s and verifies in 0.57 s; no AES or crypto hardware

projects.t: Every TI example, flashed and run by a script
projects.result: All 148 safe examples, low-power ones included: no crash, the debugger never lost the board

chains.t: TI's MSPM0 SDK, no operating system
chains.why: 167 of 170 examples build from a terminal, and all 148 that are safe to run ran with no crash

No board upstream. With the test board file, hello_world, blinky, standard CoreMark, a minimal shell, logging and Thread-Metric run, some with under 64 bytes of RAM left; Zephyr's samples as shipped need 6 to 17 kB
TI ships no example and its settings file for this board asks for 5.4 kB of RAM. With static allocation a blink uses 1 kB, 11 small tasks fit, and a task switch takes 12 to 16 microseconds
TI's SDK has no TI Drivers for this chip, only DriverLib
Plain C and the G3507's AI model libraries ran unchanged; only 22 of 270 G3507 SDK examples build after changing the device, most stopped by one SysConfig setting

40 of 91 C1104 examples build after changing the device, 57 with pins unlocked; the 51 that passed the safety check ran with no crash, but none lit an LED: they toggle the C1104 board's LED pin, which here is the light sensor

good_for: Small sensors and controllers that read light, temperature or a voltage with the analog parts on the chip
Learning bare-metal C with TI's examples: 156 build from a terminal and every safe one ran
Very small AI models in software: an 8k-parameter model ran; 30k did not link (suspected RAM limit)
Cost-sensitive designs: the chip is $0.65 in thousands
not_for: Anything with a radio: it has none
Bigger Zephyr apps: no board upstream, and Zephyr's samples as shipped need 6 to 17 kB of RAM; trimmed, a shell fits with 48 bytes left
Fast encryption: no AES hardware; a P-256 signature takes 0.5 s in software
Programs with logging, float printf or big buffers: 4 kB of RAM goes fast
Arduino or PlatformIO: no MSPM0 core exists

instead.why: 32 kB of RAM and a board in upstream Zephyr; Zephyr's blinky runs on it
32 kB of RAM; the 33k-weight model that does not fit here runs on it, 20 of 20 right

buy: $20.56 at TI.com for one board (2026-10-08). The debug probe is on the board, so one USB cable does power, flashing and the serial port.
gotchas: The chip's temperature sensor reads about -165 °C
Suspected: an early-sample factory calibration that is wrong; not confirmed on this chip. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: wrong factory trim).** Use the board's thermistor
The out-of-box demo is silent on the serial port
It waits for MessagePack commands that end in a newline, and its GUI needs a request to TI sales. **Tag: Tool or docs.** The commands are in the FAQ
A program passes its checks, then prints garbage or faults
TI's examples reserve 256 bytes of stack, and printf with %f alone needs over 400. **Tag: TI example default.** Raise the stack in the linker file
Every Zephyr image that fills RAM stops at boot with `***** HARD FAULT *****`
Zephyr's default C library heap writes past the end of RAM when only a few bytes are left. **Tag: Third-party behavior.** Set CONFIG_COMMON_LIBC_MALLOC_ARENA_SIZE=0
Only 13 of the 32 interrupt lines exist on this chip, and pending any other does nothing. **Tag: Chip limit.** Borrow an unused peripheral's line

ai_cost.headline: One AI-assisted run, with ten parallel helpers, brought this board up, ran every test on this page and wrote it up. It took one day in three sittings and about $114 to $129 of AI use at list price. The only hands-on steps after plugging it in were one jumper wire and two jumper moves for the UART test, and one power cycle.
